new_packages.label: פְּשִׁיטוּת וּתְמִימוּת
new_packages.reason: The torah's core teaching is that authentic Judaism consists of simple, wholehearted worship. Three concepts share the same essential nature: simple worship (avodot peshtutot), Shabbat zemirot, and peshitut/temimut. They are all expressions of the same reality — serving HaShem with sincerity rather than sophistication. Zemirot and techinnot are specific manifestations (bechinat) of peshitut in practice.

proposed_bechina_edges.reason: Simple worship IS simplicity/wholeheartedness in action — they are the same essence.
Singing zemirot on Shabbat is a quintessential expression of peshitut — the same quality manifest in practice.
Zemirot are explicitly listed as one of the simple worships (avodot peshtutot) — same domain.

source_quotes: עִקָּר הַיַּהֲדוּת הוּא בִּפְשִׁיטוּת וּבִתְמִימוּת גָּמוּר, בְּלִי שׁוּם חָכְמוֹת
הָיָה אוֹהֵב מְאֹד אֶת הָעֲבוֹדוֹת הַפְּשׁוּטוֹת שֶׁל סְתָם בְּנֵי־אָדָם
הָיָה מַזְהִיר וּמוֹכִיחַ אוֹתָנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים לְזַמֵּר זְמִירוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת

new_packages.label: חָכָם בְּעֵינָיו
new_packages.reason: The torah identifies 'one who is wise in his own eyes' as the counterforce to peshitut — someone too sophisticated for simple worship. This is the evil mirror of Package 1. However, this is a single-concept component and since there are no other evil-polarity concepts to group it with, it stands as a minimal evil mirror notation rather than a full package.
merge_notes: Single-node component. Could be absorbed into Package 1 as its evil counterpoint, but keeping it separate preserves the polarity distinction. As a single node with no bechina connections it does not technically qualify as a full package — listed here to document the evil mirror structure.
source_quotes: הָיָה מַקְפִּיד וְכוֹעֵס מְאֹד עַל מִי שֶׁהוּא חָכָם בְּעֵינָיו וְאֵינוֹ מִתְאַמֵּץ לְזַמֵּר זְמִירוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת

observations: Torah #104 has zero edges in the existing dataset. It is a narrative/behavioral teaching rather than a conceptual Torah — Rebbe Nachman's love for simple worship and his insistence on singing zemirot. Despite the non-theoretical nature, the text contains a clear cluster of 3 bechina-connected concepts around simplicity/wholeheartedness (peshitut, avodot peshtutot, zemirot Shabbat), qualifying as a new package. The evil mirror is minimal — 'chacham be'einav' (wise in one's own eyes) as the single opposing concept. The good/evil polarity is clear: peshitut (good) vs. false sophistication (evil). Note: this torah is more anecdotal/hanhagah in style (Tinyana #104), so the conceptual density is lower than a standard Torah.
